newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Players await PPI, payrolls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Players await PPI, payrolls.

text.p: With the holiday hoopla finally over, U.S. credit market participants will focus on top-tier economic data during the first full workweek of 1997.
And many analysts predicted the news would likely generate excitement in Treasuries, especially the heavily-watched payrolls data set for release on Friday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

"The recent numbers have shown that the economy has been performing well in excess of the (Federal Reserve's) desired pace," said Dan Seto, senior economist at The Nikko Securities Co International Inc.
"That may be all fine and good for some of the Fed officials as long as inflation is kept in check ... that is why (Friday's) wage number is so important," Seto said.
Kicking off the week, November factory orders and consumer credit are slated for release on Tuesday and Wednesday, respectively.
Also scheduled on Wednesday, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin will speak about the economy at a Mortgage Bankers Association of America conference in New York.
But many experts said the main attraction will be the release of producer prices and payrolls data on Thursday and Friday, respectively.
Christopher Low, senior economist at HSBC Markets Inc, said the risk for the December payroll report is on the higher side.
"Part of it is the weather," Low said, explaining that the weather "depressed" the report in November when payrolls only rose 118,000.
In addition, Nikko's Seto said last month's payrolls number was "artificially low" because of the late Thanksgiving holiday.
"So we're going to get some of a bounce back here," he said.
HSBC's Low calculated about 60,000 of the November payroll number was weather-related. He contends many economists have built in a partial reversal of that weakness, but not a complete reversal.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, payrolls growth of 192,000, an unemployment rate of 5.30 percent and a 0.2 percent rise in average hourly earnings.
Yet Low said, "I think that there is a distinct possibility that you could see a payroll rise in excess of 250,000."
"If that happens, the market (will) clearly not be prepared for that," he added.
Preceding payrolls data in time but not in importance is the Producer Price Index (PPI), which is expected to show a similar reading to last month.

On average, experts forecast overall December PPI rose 0.3 percent after posting a 0.4 percent gain in the previous month. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, PPI is seen advancing 0.1 percent, the same expansion rate as November.
"I just don't see any scope here for core inflation that is significant," said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.
Kretzmer noted that computer prices are expected to continue to decline and last month's rise in auto prices are likely to reverse.
He said a core of 0.1 percent will be favorable for the credit markets. But the market will react poorly with a core reading of above 0.2 percent.
"The wildcard is energy ... as usual this year," he said.

Late Friday the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was trading 1/32 lower at 96-29/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The 10-year was up 1/32 at 99-29/32 to yield 6.51 percent. The fed funds rate is expected to open Monday at 5-5/16.
(( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1562))
